prospect.name: Javier
prospect.occupation: Professional online poker player, playing eight to ten hours a day seated. Has a standing-capable desk and a separate office about 15 minutes from home. Started playing at college in the United States in 2004 during the post-Moneymaker poker boom.
prospect.family_status: Has a 10-year-old son and a girlfriend. Frames his window with his son sharply — 'he's got probably four more playing years in him, and then he's just gonna forget about me'.
prospect.training_background: Boxes three times a week and walks 5,000-8,000 steps a day. Previously did calisthenics via Frank Medrano's online programme and got 'really shredded' at 68 kg, but injured himself because the programme was generic and gave no form feedback. Has run carnivore and other diets. Usual weight 72-73 kg; currently at his heaviest ever, 83.5 kg (roughly 85 a month ago), at 1.80 m.
prospect.medical: Chronic lower back pain for several years, rated 6-7 out of 10 on bad days and variable. Shoulder stiffness with restricted overhead and lateral range — 'there's some movements that I can't go up' — noticeable when boxing but not in daily life. Has an appointment in Dallas in September with a viral chiropractor for the back. Smokes daily and links it to appetite: 'if I don't smoke, then I get no cravings at all... if I smoke, I'll get the munchies'. Currently eight days into keto, having had four days of keto flu.

signals: Successful in his field and the rest of life is in order — a poker pro living off the game, with health as the single lagging area: 'I just wasn't taking care of myself'
Aspiration is beyond his former self, not back to it: 'I just want to be in the best shape of my life, because I know if I'm in the best shape of my life, then I can live longer'
Zero price resistance — accepted $6,000 within seconds of hearing it and asked only whether it was one payment or monthly
Already self-optimising before the call: eight days into keto, running an eight-hour eating window, boxing three times a week, no sugar or soda

Counter-signal toward the_rebuilder: he is at the heaviest weight of his life and in chronic pain, and describes himself as having gone 'skinny fat, and now I'm just fat' — but the drift was lifestyle over a few months, not illness or a hard season

Later, during the presentation: 'we're not going to start with super heavy weights, it just comes down to building foundation, getting the understanding of how to actually do the form', reinforced with a poker analogy about starting at five-dollar stakes before raising them.

notable.note: The easiest close in the batch and, oddly, the weakest execution of Phase 11. Zero price resistance — the prospect had declared 'I'm locked in' and 'I'm 100% committed' twenty minutes before the number was mentioned, and accepted $6,000 in one exchange. Yet no money was collected. The card was at an office fifteen minutes away, the rep floated the idea of fetching it, then accepted a two-hour deferral and booked a second call to do what could have been done in the moment. No agreement was mentioned at all, no signature, no welcome email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire — compare the Scott Hamilton call in this batch where all of that ran cleanly. Two other things to flag. He disclosed a shoulder with restricted overhead range and several years of chronic back pain severe enough that he is flying to Dallas in September to see a chiropractor, and he named the doubt himself — whether he can even hold a kettlebell overhead. The rep answered it with reassurance about Trevor's own injury history rather than any assessment or clearance. And he volunteered that he smokes daily and that it drives his cravings; it was probed for frequency in a nutrition context and never treated as a health factor.
